answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once, which means an operator running a synchronised farm is punished proportionally to the size of the group he synchronised. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. A farm holds one timber style of behaviour, one atlas signature, and eats one haven penalty; the timber is per identity, but the atlas and the haven are what make the group collectively liable. Uniform behaviour forfeits the whole group's collateral at once.
